varieties.name: Golden Bantam
varieties.description: Golden Bantam is a classic corn variety that has been a favorite among gardeners since the early 1900s for its sweet and flavorful kernels. The golden-yellow ears are tender and ideal for fresh eating, grilling, and roasting. With a tall upright growth habit, Golden Bantam corn is a reliable heirloom choice for home gardens and provides a delicious addition to summer meals.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, especially during tasseling and ear development
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Nitrogen-rich fertilizer at planting and when 12 inches tall

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, rich corn flavor, tender and creamy

fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate for 2-3 days or freeze

varieties.fun_fact: Golden Bantam, introduced in the early 1900s, is one of the first widely popular sweet corn varieties, revolutionizing the way people enjoyed corn on the cob and setting the standard for sweet corn flavor.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Golden Bantam in blocks of at least 4 rows rather than single rows to ensure good pollination by wind. Sow seeds 1-2 inches deep when soil reaches 60°F. Harvest when silks turn brown and kernels are plump and milky when pierced.

varieties.name: Peaches and Cream
varieties.description: Peaches and Cream corn is a popular bi-color variety known for its sweet and juicy kernels. The ears have a delightful combination of yellow and white kernels, making them visually appealing and delicious. With a tall upright growth habit and excellent flavor, Peaches and Cream is a versatile choice for various culinary applications.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent moisture during ear development
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting and side-dress when knee-high

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Very sweet, reminiscent of peaches and cream, juicy

fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Best fresh; refrigerate for 2-3 days or freeze

varieties.fun_fact: Peaches and Cream corn is prized for its deliciously sweet flavor, reminiscent of summer peaches, making it a favorite among corn enthusiasts. The bi-color kernels add beautiful visual appeal to any dish!
varieties.planting_tip: Plant in blocks for better pollination. Water deeply and consistently, especially during silk and tassel formation. Harvest when kernels squirt milky juice when punctured - this is the 'milk stage' when flavor is at its peak.

varieties.name: Country Gentleman
varieties.description: Country Gentleman corn is a classic white heirloom variety known for its tender and flavorful kernels arranged in an irregular, shoepeg pattern. The ears have a refined, creamy taste, making them a favorite for fresh eating and culinary applications. With a tall upright growth habit, Country Gentleman is a reliable choice for home gardens seeking old-fashioned corn flavor.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, especially during hot weather and ear fill
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting and when plants are knee-high

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, creamy, refined flavor with tender kernels

varieties.fun_fact: Country Gentleman corn, also known as 'Shoepeg Corn,' is valued for its unique kernel arrangement, with kernels packed in irregular zigzag rows resembling the shape of a shoepeg or shoe nail, rather than the typical straight rows.
varieties.planting_tip: This heirloom variety has exceptional flavor but takes longer to mature. Plant in warm soil and ensure good pollination by planting in blocks. The irregular kernel pattern is normal and indicates authentic Country Gentleman corn!

varieties.name: Glass Gem
varieties.description: Glass Gem corn is a unique and stunning ornamental variety known for its vibrant and multicolored kernels that resemble translucent gemstones. The ears display a rainbow of colors including blue, purple, pink, green, yellow, and red. This flint corn variety is primarily grown for decorative purposes but can also be ground into cornmeal. With a tall upright growth habit, Glass Gem adds spectacular color to garden landscapes.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1 inch per week, can tolerate some dryness once established
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Not for fresh eating; can be ground into sweet, nutty cornmeal

fruit_characteristics.fruit_color: Multicolored (rainbow of blues, purples, pinks, greens, yellows, reds)
fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Excellent for long-term storage and display when fully dried

varieties.fun_fact: Glass Gem corn gained international popularity for its breathtakingly beautiful kernels, which can display a wide range of translucent colors resembling gemstones. It was developed by Carl Barnes, a part-Cherokee farmer who bred it to reconnect with his heritage!
varieties.planting_tip: Allow ears to fully mature and dry on the stalk for the most vibrant colors. Isolate from sweet corn by at least 250 feet to prevent cross-pollination. Harvest when husks are completely dry and kernels are hard. The color intensity increases as the corn dries.

varieties.name: Dakota Black
varieties.description: Dakota Black corn is a distinctive heirloom variety with dark black to deep purple kernels, adding a unique and dramatic touch to both culinary dishes and decorative use. This flint corn has a rich, earthy flavor when ground into flour or meal. With a tall upright growth habit, Dakota Black is a standout choice for gardeners seeking something unique and historically significant.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1 inch per week, drought-tolerant once established
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Rich, earthy, slightly sweet when ground; nutty undertones

fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Excellent for long-term storage when dried properly

varieties.fun_fact: Dakota Black corn is prized for its deep black kernels, which provide a visually striking element to gardens and culinary creations. This ancient variety was traditionally grown by Native American tribes in the Great Plains region!
varieties.planting_tip: Allow ears to dry completely on the stalk until husks are brown and papery. This flint corn requires full maturity for best color and flavor. Grind the dried kernels into a beautiful purple-black flour rich in antioxidants. Isolate from sweet corn to maintain purity.

varieties.name: Silver Queen
varieties.description: Silver Queen is one of the most beloved white sweet corn varieties, famous for its exceptionally sweet flavor and tender kernels. The large ears are filled with plump, creamy white kernels that remain sweet and tender longer than many varieties. Silver Queen has been a garden favorite since the 1950s and is considered by many to be the standard by which all other white corn is measured.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent moisture crucial
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder - nitrogen-rich fertilizer at planting and side-dress twice

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Exceptionally sweet, tender, creamy with classic white corn flavor

fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Best fresh; sweetness holds well; refrigerate for up to 3 days

varieties.fun_fact: Silver Queen has been a garden staple since 1956 and is often called the 'Queen of White Corn'! It's so popular that some gardeners won't grow any other variety, and many farm stands sell out of Silver Queen first!
varieties.planting_tip: Silver Queen needs warm soil (at least 65°F) to germinate well. Plant in blocks of at least 4 rows for best pollination. This variety loves heat and performs exceptionally well in hot summer climates. Pick ears when silks are brown and dry for peak sweetness.

varieties.name: Honey Select Hybrid
varieties.description: Honey Select is a premium tricolor hybrid sweet corn variety that produces stunning ears with a mix of yellow, white, and bi-color kernels. This sugary-enhanced (SE) corn offers exceptional sweetness that holds well after harvest, making it perfect for fresh eating and market sales. Honey Select combines excellent flavor with strong disease resistance and adaptability to various growing conditions. The tall, vigorous plants produce uniform ears with excellent tip fill.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent moisture during ear development
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Balanced fertilizer at planting and side-dress when knee-high

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Exceptionally sweet, tender-crisp texture, holds sweetness for 3-5 days after picking

fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Excellent - sweetness holds for 3-5 days refrigerated

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Honey Select is a sugary-enhanced (SE) corn, which means it converts less sugar to starch after harvest compared to traditional sweet corn, keeping it sweeter longer! The tricolor ears make every harvest a surprise with their beautiful mix of yellow, white, and bi-colored kernels.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Honey Select in warm soil (60°F+) in blocks of at least 4 rows for best pollination. Water deeply and consistently, especially during tasseling and silk formation. This variety has excellent disease resistance and performs well in various conditions. Harvest window is longer than standard varieties - ears maintain quality for several days at peak ripeness.

varieties.name: Bodacious
varieties.description: Bodacious is a highly productive hybrid yellow sweet corn variety known for its outstanding flavor, large ears, and reliable performance. This sugary-enhanced corn produces hefty 8-9 inch ears with excellent tip fill and plump, sweet kernels. Bodacious is prized for its strong stalks that resist lodging, consistent yields even in challenging conditions, and extended harvest window. It's a favorite among both home gardeners and commercial growers.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, especially during ear development
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder - nitrogen-rich fertilizer at planting and side-dress when knee-high

tolerances.heat_tolerance: Excellent - performs well in hot conditions

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Intensely sweet, rich corn flavor with tender-crisp texture

fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Very good - holds sweetness well for 3-4 days refrigerated

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Bodacious has won numerous taste tests and awards for its exceptional flavor! It's known for producing consistently large, well-filled ears even in less-than-ideal conditions, earning its reputation as one of the most reliable sweet corn varieties available.
varieties.planting_tip: Plant Bodacious in blocks of at least 4 rows for optimal pollination. Strong stalks resist wind damage better than many varieties. Water deeply during ear development for best kernel fill. This variety has excellent disease resistance, making it a low-maintenance choice. Succession plant every 2 weeks for continuous harvest through summer.

varieties.name: Stowell's Evergreen
varieties.description: Stowell's Evergreen is a legendary heirloom white corn variety dating back to 1848, famous for its incredibly long harvest window and excellent keeping quality. This tall, vigorous variety produces large ears that remain in prime eating condition longer than almost any other corn. The name 'Evergreen' refers to the fact that the kernels stay tender and sweet for an extended period. It's a favorite for late-season planting and successive harvests.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent moisture important
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder - nitrogen-rich fertilizer at planting and side-dress when knee-high

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, rich, old-fashioned corn flavor - tender and stays sweet longer than modern varieties

fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Exceptional - ears remain in eating condition for 7-10 days, excellent for canning

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Stowell's Evergreen was developed in 1848 by Nathan Stowell of New Jersey and has been grown continuously for over 175 years! It revolutionized corn growing because the ears stayed tender and sweet much longer than other varieties of the time, earning the name 'Evergreen.'
varieties.planting_tip: This tall variety needs warm soil (65°F+) and full sun. Plant in blocks for good pollination. The extended harvest window means ears can be picked over a longer period without becoming tough. Excellent for succession planting and late-season crops. The tall stalks can handle some wind but may need support in very windy areas.

varieties.name: Painted Mountain
varieties.description: Painted Mountain is a unique, cold-hardy flour corn variety bred specifically for short growing seasons and harsh climates. This stunning ornamental corn displays a rainbow of colors including burgundy, gold, orange, blue, and white kernels. Developed in Montana, Painted Mountain matures faster than most corn varieties and can germinate in soil as cool as 50°F. It's perfect for grinding into nutritious, colorful flour or cornmeal and makes beautiful decorative displays.

growth_info.spacing: 10-12 inches apart in rows 24-30 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1 inch per week, drought tolerant once established
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Moderate feeder - balanced fertilizer at planting

harvest_storage.typical_yield: 1-3 small to medium ears per stalk

tolerances.cold_tolerance: Excellent - best cold tolerance of any corn

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Sweet, nutty, rich flavor when ground into flour - slightly sweet with complex undertones

fruit_characteristics.fruit_color: Multicolored (burgundy, gold, orange, blue, white, purple)
fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Excellent for long-term storage when dried, high in protein and antioxidants

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Painted Mountain was bred specifically for growing at high elevations with short seasons! It can germinate in soil as cool as 50°F and matures in just 80-90 days, making it perfect for northern gardens, high-altitude growing, and short growing seasons where other corn varieties fail.
varieties.planting_tip: Perfect for short-season climates! Plant as soon as soil reaches 50°F - much earlier than other corn. Space closer than traditional corn due to compact size. Excellent for northern zones 3-5. Allow ears to dry completely on stalks. Grind dried kernels into colorful, nutritious flour high in protein and antioxidants. Can be grown in areas other corn varieties can't!

varieties.name: Incredible Hybrid
varieties.description: Incredible is an aptly named supersweet (SH2) hybrid corn variety that delivers extraordinary sweetness and tender-crisp texture. This yellow corn produces large, well-filled ears that stay sweet for an extended period after harvest. Incredible is prized by both home gardeners and market growers for its exceptional eating quality, consistent performance, and superior disease resistance. The sugars are 2-3 times higher than standard sweet corn varieties.

growth_info.spacing: 12-18 inches apart in rows 30-36 inches apart

care_requirements.water_requirement: 1-1.5 inches per week, consistent moisture crucial for supersweet varieties
care_requirements.feeding_requirement: Heavy feeder - nitrogen-rich fertilizer at planting and side-dress when knee-high

tolerances.cold_tolerance: Poor - needs warm soil (70°F+) to germinate

flavor_characteristics.flavor_profile: Incredibly sweet - 2-3x sweeter than standard sweet corn, tender-crisp texture, holds sweetness for 7-10 days

fruit_characteristics.storage_quality: Excellent - maintains sweetness for 7-10 days refrigerated

varieties.fun_fact: Did you know? Incredible is a supersweet (SH2) corn, meaning it has 2-3 times more sugar than standard sweet corn! It's so sweet it can be eaten raw right off the stalk. The supersweet gene also means it stays sweet much longer after harvest - up to 10 days refrigerated!
varieties.planting_tip: IMPORTANT: Supersweet corn must be isolated from other corn types by at least 250 feet or planted 2 weeks earlier/later to prevent cross-pollination. Needs warm soil (70°F+) to germinate - don't rush planting. Water consistently for best kernel development. The exceptional sweetness and long-lasting quality make this ideal for market growers. Harvest when silks are brown and dry.
